label: Schemes: Local Algebra Becomes Geometry
notes: Open by naming the chapter goal: schemes keep algebraic information that classical varieties tend to discard. The section strip is the whole lecture in miniature, moving from sheaf gluing and prime points through morphisms, divisors, differentials, and formal completions.

label: The Nine-Part Arc
notes: Use this slide as a contract with the audience. Each section contributes one grammatical move: local data, affine spectra, scheme properties, control of morphisms, sheaf modules, codimension-one bookkeeping, projective maps, first-order behavior, and infinite thickenings.

label: Sheaves Glue Local Data
notes: Treat the notebook image as a gluing board rather than a topological picture. The key teaching point is that local sections are not independent pieces: after restriction to overlaps they must agree, and the sheaf axiom says the compatible family has a unique glued section.

label: Stalks Are Local Tests
notes: A stalk is the algebraic microscope at a point. Explain that germs forget behavior away from the point, then stress the practical theorem: many sheaf questions can be checked stalk by stalk, especially whether a morphism of sheaves is an isomorphism.

label: Spec A: Prime Ideals As Points
notes: Read the specialization poset from generic primes toward closed primes. The finite model is not a full spectrum, but it makes the reversal visible: inclusion of prime ideals becomes geometric specialization, and irreducible components acquire generic points.

label: Principal Opens Localize Rings
notes: This is the local algebra engine of affine schemes. Principal opens are simultaneously topological neighborhoods and ring localizations, so intersections and restrictions can be computed with the formulas D(f) cap D(g) equals D(fg) and O(D(f)) equals A_f.

label: A Scheme Is Glued From Affines
notes: Move from one affine chart to an atlas. The diagram emphasizes that a scheme is not just a union of affine pieces: the overlap identifications must agree on triple overlaps, which is the cocycle condition that makes the glued object independent of chart order.

label: Morphisms Reverse Rings
notes: Make contravariance concrete. A geometric morphism from Spec B to Spec A is encoded by pulling functions back from A to B, and the point map sends a prime of B to its preimage in A. This is the affine prototype for morphisms of schemes.

label: Reduced, Irreducible, Integral
notes: Use the nilpotent image to separate point sets from function rings. Reduced removes nilpotents, irreducible asks for one generic component, and integral combines both; on an affine chart this corresponds to a domain condition. This is the first property checkpoint.

label: Subschemes, Products, Fibers
notes: The left half explains closed subschemes as quotient rings rather than simply subsets. The right half gives the pullback square habit: fibers and products are universal ways to compare families over a base. Keep the universal property in view.

label: Separatedness Is Diagonal Control
notes: Separatedness is the scheme-theoretic version of uniqueness of limits. The doubled-origin picture shows what fails when two specializations are forced to share a generic part, while the closed diagonal criterion gives the clean structural test.

label: Properness Is Complete Lifting
notes: The valuative criterion packages compactness-like behavior for schemes. Separatedness gives uniqueness of a lift, while properness adds existence: a map defined generically over a discrete valuation ring extends over the special point. The picture is a lifting test, not a computation.

label: Modules Become Sheaves
notes: Explain quasi-coherent sheaves by starting with a familiar module. On Spec A, the tilde construction has global sections M and restricts to M_f on D(f), so the sheaf records the same algebra chart by chart.

label: Divisors Track Codimension One
notes: Present divisors as a ledger at codimension-one points. The principal divisor check on P1 is intentionally small: div(t) has one zero and one pole, so its degree is zero, matching the notebook sanity check. This anchors the bookkeeping.

label: Projective Morphisms From Sections
notes: Sections of an invertible sheaf become homogeneous coordinates for a map to projective space. The warning is just as important as the construction: if all chosen sections vanish at a point, the projective coordinate is undefined.

label: Differentials Are Universal Derivations
notes: Use the universal property as the definition that makes every derivation factor through differentials. The cusp calculation is a local sanity check: differentiating y squared minus x cubed gives the relation minus three dx plus two dy at the point (1,1).

label: Formal Schemes Keep Every Thickening
notes: Return to the nilpotent tower and now read it as a limit object. A formal completion does not add new ordinary points; it records every infinitesimal neighborhood of the closed subscheme at once. The tower is the geometry.

label: Scheme-Theoretic Grammar
notes: Close by naming the reusable proof pattern. Check the claim on affine charts, translate the computation through sheaves on overlaps, then prove that the invariant is independent of the chosen cover. This is the grammar students should reuse.
